stem.text: A cyclist pedals along a raised horizontal track. At the end of the track, he travels horizontally into the air and onto a track that is vertically $2.0\,\text{m}$ lower.

stem.alt: Diagram of a cyclist leaving a higher horizontal track along a dashed curved path onto a lower horizontal track, with labels higher horizontal track, lower horizontal track, 2.0 m, 6.0 m and v.

stem.text: The cyclist travels a horizontal distance of $6.0\,\text{m}$ in the air. Air resistance is negligible.
What is the horizontal velocity $v$ of the cyclist at the end of the higher track?
